name: Progress
description: Progress wraps the native HTMLProgressElement in a labeled container and supports determinate, indeterminate, and milestone-marked states.

elements.name: label
elements.description: The accessible label displayed above or beside the progress bar.

elements.name: value
elements.description: The current numeric progress value. Omit it to render an indeterminate progress state.

elements.name: max
elements.description: The maximum progress value. Defaults to 100; invalid or non-positive values are normalized to 1.

elements.name: trackHeight
elements.description: Sets the progress track height using a CSS length. The default is based on the component font size.

elements.name: size
elements.description: Sets the component scale to sm, md, or lg.

elements.name: labelPosition
elements.description: Places the label at the top (default) or left of the progress bar.

elements.name: preciseDots
elements.description: Adds markers at numeric positions. Each item requires a value, accepts an optional React label, and supports optional span properties through props. Values outside the range are ignored.

elements.name: regularDots
elements.description: Adds evenly distributed React markers from the start to the end of the progress bar. Use either regularDots or preciseDots, not both.

elements.name: labelProps
elements.description: Passes native label properties to the visible label element.

elements.name: containerProps
elements.description: Passes native div properties to the outer field container.

elements.name: dotsProps
elements.description: Passes native div properties to the container holding milestone markers.

elements.name: Native progress properties
elements.description: Native progress properties such as id, className, value, max, and aria-* attributes are forwarded to the progress element.

accessibility.general: The component uses a native progress element, preserving native progress semantics for determinate and indeterminate states. The visible label is associated with the progress element through for/id.
elements: Provide a meaningful label so the progress indicator has an accessible name. If no visible label is rendered, provide an accessible name through the native progress attributes.
Omit value only when completion is genuinely unknown; the native element then exposes an indeterminate state.
Use preciseDots or regularDots as supplemental visual milestones. Their labels do not replace the numeric progress value for assistive technologies.
Keep value within the intended range defined by max; the component clamps out-of-range values before rendering.
The indeterminate animation is disabled when the user prefers reduced motion, and forced-colors mode preserves a visible native progress fallback.
